meta.source: Ergast/Jolpica results, with team lineages curated in scripts/f1/lineages.py

bases.note: The only 2026 team with no facility in England.
The McLaren Technology Centre opened in 2004; the team had been in Woking since 1981.
Ken Tyrrell's works, at Long Reach between Ockham and Ripley. Period directories render the same address as both, which is a postal variant rather than a second site.
Built for BAR's 1999 debut by Adrian Reynard's Reynard Motorsport, and the same building through Honda, Brawn and Mercedes.
Mercedes-AMG High Performance Powertrains. Engines only.

eras.name: British American Racing
eras.note: BAR bought Tyrrell's entry in 1998 and moved the operation to a new Brackley factory. The purchase of the entry, not just the assets, is what makes this one organisation rather than two.

eras.name: Honda Racing F1
eras.note: Honda bought the team outright for 2006. Distinct from the 1964-68 Honda works team, which is filed separately.

eras.name: Brawn GP
eras.note: Ross Brawn's management buyout after Honda withdrew in late 2008. One season, both titles, then sold to Mercedes.

eras.name: Mercedes
eras.note: Distinct from the 1954-55 Mercedes-Benz works team, filed separately.

bases.note: One site, three owners: Stewart from 1997, Jaguar from 2000, Red Bull from 2005.

eras.name: Jaguar Racing
eras.note: Ford bought Stewart in 1999 and rebranded it Jaguar for 2000.

eras.name: Red Bull Racing
eras.note: Red Bull bought Jaguar from Ford in November 2004 for a reported one dollar plus a commitment to invest.

lineages.name: Williams

bases.note: Two buildings: a former carpet warehouse on Station Road from 1977, then purpose-built premises on Basil Hill Road from 1984.
The wind tunnel moved on 28 April 1996 and the factory was formally opened that October.

eras.name: Williams
eras.note: Ergast runs this record from 1975, but Williams Grand Prix Engineering was founded in 1977 and first raced in 1978. The 1975-76 entries are Frank Williams Racing Cars, the earlier team he sold to Walter Wolf. Left together because the constructors' record treats them as one; the distinction is recorded here rather than acted on.

lineages.note: Ergast runs this record from 1975, but Williams Grand Prix Engineering was founded in 1977 and first raced in 1978. The 1975-76 entries are Frank Williams Racing Cars, the earlier team he sold to Walter Wolf. Left together because the constructors' record treats them as one; the distinction is recorded here rather than acted on.

bases.note: Chapman's original works in north London, behind a stable yard.
A former RAF bomber station. Lotus laid its test track on the perimeter runways, which is why the place is a village and an aerodrome at once.

eras.name: Team Lotus
eras.note: Ergast files Colin Chapman's team under seven chassis-engine records. They are one team, and the wins only make sense added together.

bases.note: Whiteways Technical Centre, occupied over the winter of 1991-92 and unchanged through Benetton, Renault, Lotus and Alpine.
Renault's F1 engine works, and the reason the team read as French. Renault closed the programme after 2025 and Alpine runs Mercedes power units from 2026, which leaves Enstone as the single base.

eras.name: Renault F1 Team
eras.note: Renault bought Benetton in 2000 and ran under its own name from 2002. Distinct from the 1977-85 Renault works team, filed separately.

eras.name: Lotus F1 Team
eras.note: Genii Capital's renaming of the same Enstone entrant. No relation to Team Lotus, nor to the 2010-11 Lotus Racing that became Caterham.

bases.note: Motor Racing Developments, near Weybridge.
Raymond Mays's works behind Eastgate House, with a private test track on the disused Folkingham aerodrome a few miles away.
A garage behind the family home. The team that put the engine behind the driver and ended the front-engined era worked out of a suburban high street.
The former Gordini works, to which all Renault racing moved at the end of 1976. Where the turbo engine entered Formula 1.

eras.name: Équipe Renault Elf
eras.note: The Viry-Châtillon works team that introduced the turbo engine to Formula 1. Unconnected to the Enstone team that later carried the name.

bases.note: Usually written as Vichy, the neighbouring town. The plant at Abrest is still Ligier's.

The move year is not settled. grandprix.com and f1technical both place it in 1988; the 1990 and 1991 dates that circulate elsewhere appear to belong to the circuit's reconstruction and the French Grand Prix moving there, which are different events.
Alfa Corse, at the Portello plant.
Autodelta.
Euroracing took the entry over from Autodelta for 1983.

eras.name: Alfa Romeo SpA
eras.note: The Portello works team that won the first two drivers' championships with Farina and Fangio, then withdrew.

eras.name: Alfa Romeo private entries
eras.note: Two scattered mid-sixties entries Ergast files under the same record. They are neither the works team nor Autodelta, and are kept with the marque rather than assigned to an organisation we cannot name.

eras.name: Autodelta / Euroracing Alfa Romeo
eras.note: Alfa's return as a constructor, run by Autodelta and then Euroracing. Unconnected to the 2019-23 Alfa Romeo, which was Sauber.

bases.note: Viale Ciro Menotti, where Maserati still is.

eras.name: Matra
eras.note: THE ARGUABLE MERGE. The Matra-Ford entries of 1968-69, including Stewart's 1969 title, were run by Ken Tyrrell's Matra International, not by Matra Sports. The chassis constructor is credited here because that is what the constructors' championship recognised, but the ENTRANT was the team that became Tyrrell, and a reader who wants those wins under Tyrrell is not wrong.

bases.note: The Daimler-Benz Rennabteilung at Untertuerkheim.

eras.name: Mercedes-Benz
eras.note: The W196 works team. Two seasons, two drivers' titles, withdrawn after Le Mans 1955 and unconnected to the Brackley team that carries the name now.

bases.note: The racing shop was at Cox Green. Acton in west London was Vandervell Products, the bearing company that paid for it, and is often given as the team's address by mistake.

lineages.name: Aston Martin

bases.note: One site continuously since Jordan built it in 1991, through Midland, Spyker, Force India and Racing Point. The AMR Technology Campus that replaced it opened in 2023 on the same land.

eras.name: MF1 Racing
eras.note: Midland bought Jordan in 2005 and ran as MF1 for 2006. Ergast splits the single 2006 season across two records; both are claimed here.

eras.name: Force India
eras.note: Vijay Mallya's consortium bought Spyker in October 2007.

eras.name: Racing Point
eras.note: THE ARGUABLE LINK IN THIS CHAIN. Force India went into administration in July 2018 and Lawrence Stroll's consortium bought the ASSETS, not the company; the FIA treated the 2018 entry as two entrants and split the season's points. Recorded as continuous because the factory, the staff and the entry all carried on, but a reader who wants to cut the chain here has a real argument.

eras.name: Aston Martin
eras.note: Distinct from the 1959-60 Aston Martin works team, filed separately.

pointsNotes: The FIA docked Racing Point 15 constructors' points for copying the 2019 Mercedes brake ducts, so the championship credited 195 against 210 scored on track.

eras.name: Kurtis Kraft
eras.note: An Indianapolis chassis builder. Its five wins came in the Indy 500, which counted for the World Championship from 1950 to 1960.

bases.note: The Bennett Road premises Walter Wolf took over from Frank Williams.
Minardi's works, and the same company through Toro Rosso, AlphaTauri and Racing Bulls.
Aerodynamics and design, moved from Bicester for 2025.

eras.name: Scuderia Toro Rosso
eras.note: Red Bull bought Minardi in 2005 and renamed it for 2006. The entrant at Faenza has been the same company throughout.

bases.note: Sources give only Tokyo for the first season.
Honda Racing's European base, with the RA300 chassis built by Lola at Slough. Japan's first works team finished its Formula 1 career in Berkshire.

eras.name: Honda R&D
eras.note: Honda's first works entry, which won at Mexico in 1965 and Monza in 1967 before withdrawing. Unconnected to the 2006-08 Brackley team.

bases.note: Sauber's works since 1993, unchanged through BMW Sauber, Alfa Romeo, Stake and now Audi.
Audi F1 technical centre.
The town is not a district; the district it names is.

eras.name: BMW Sauber
eras.note: BMW bought a controlling stake in 2005 for the 2006 season.

eras.name: Sauber
eras.note: Peter Sauber bought the team back when BMW withdrew at the end of 2009.

eras.name: Alfa Romeo
eras.note: A title-sponsorship rename of the Hinwil team, not the Alfa Romeo works team of 1950-51 or 1979-85. Ergast files all three under one record; they are separated here.

eras.name: Stake F1 Team Kick Sauber
eras.note: The full entrant name, because 'Kick Sauber' is how the 2024-25 team is listed elsewhere on the site and the lookup from a valuations row has to find it.

eras.name: Audi
eras.note: Audi completed its acquisition of Sauber Holding in January 2025 and the entry runs as the Audi works team from 2026.

bases.note: An American team on paper. Tony Southgate's account places the works in a UOP-owned factory on Weedon Road in Northampton from late 1972, taken on to build the DN1.
Converted stables on Lord Hesketh's Easton Neston estate, about six miles from Silverstone.

eras.name: Anglo American Racers
eras.note: Dan Gurney's team. Its 1967 Spa win with the Eagle-Weslake remains the only championship win by an American constructor with an American driver.

bases.note: Water Eaton industrial estate, Bletchley.
Tom Walkinshaw's TWR headquarters, taken over in April 1996.

eras.name: Footwork
eras.note: Footwork bought into Arrows in 1990 and the entry ran under the Footwork name from 1991 before reverting.

bases.note: Race operations, and in practice the team's working base. Listed as the main site for that reason rather than the American headquarters.
The registered headquarters, inside Haas Automation's NASCAR campus.
Design office. The chassis itself is built by Dallara.
Toyota Motorsport GmbH, in Cologne since 1979 and the largest single facility any manufacturer has built for Formula 1 outside England.
Sources disagree between Chasetown and Trent Valley Road in Lichfield, four miles apart. Recorded as Lichfield because that is the more specific claim, but the building is unsettled.
Next to the Paul Ricard circuit.

eras.name: ATS (Auto Technisches Spezialzubehör)
eras.note: Günter Schmid's wheel company. Shares an acronym with the 1963 Italian team and nothing else; Ergast files both under one record.

bases.note: The former Arrows and Super Aguri works, taken on in January 2012.

eras.name: Lotus Racing
eras.note: Tony Fernandes's Hingham team, licensed to use the Lotus name. No relation to Team Lotus or to the Enstone Lotus F1 Team.

lineages.name: Lola

bases.note: Yeovil Road, on the Slough Trading Estate.

eras.name: Lola
eras.note: Lola built cars for several different entrants rather than running one continuous works team, so this record is a marque, not an organisation.

lineages.note: Lola built cars for several different entrants rather than running one continuous works team, so this record is a marque, not an organisation.

bases.note: Prost bought Ligier and inherited the Magny-Cours works.
Where the cars were actually built. Scuderia Italia entered them; Dallara designed and made them.
Scuderia Italia's own offices.
Consolidated into the Caja Magica complex for the final season.
HRT never had one base. Offices in Murcia, a technical centre at Alzira near Valencia, and a 2010 car designed and built by Dallara in Italy.
The Euroracing works, two years after Alfa Romeo left them.
Registered in Tokyo, built in Oxfordshire, in the factory Arrows left.
Near Ludwigshafen.
Peter Monteverdi bought the team in 1990 and moved it to Switzerland before it folded; no source names the Swiss town, so it is not recorded.
Acres industrial estate.
The 2026 car is being run from Silverstone while Fishers is completed, so the newest American team's first season is an English operation.
The designated headquarters, still under construction through 2026.

eras.name: Embassy Hill
eras.note: Graham Hill's Embassy Hill team, ended by the 1975 air crash.

eras.name: ATS (Automobili Turismo e Sport)
eras.note: Founded by Ferrari engineers who walked out in the 1961 palace revolt. One season.

eras.name: Aston Martin
eras.note: The DBR4 works entry, six races and no points. Unconnected to the Silverstone team that carries the name now.
